levelsPanel.title: The 5 grades of success
levelsPanel.text: The more precise your stroke, the further your gesture reaches.
levelsPanel.miss: Miss: no effect, and your streak starts over.

fin.texte: Three gestures. Not one more. And one day, you'll teach them to someone else.

cinematique_ouverture.texte: In Pierrelune, every morning begins with a lesson.
The Circle guards you. The Triangle fights for you. The Tap connects you to others. Three gestures, Aldric. Not one more.
And when I know them by heart, Master?
Then you'll have to teach them to someone else. It's the only way not to lose them.
That morning, a grey mist came down from the mountain. And the master never finished his lesson.

dialogue_avant.texte: Figures at the village gates… They have no faces!
Aldric! The signs, just as I taught you!

dialogue_apres.texte: Master? Master, where are you?
No one answers. The mist has carried away the master's voice.

dialogue_avant.texte: Night falls on Pierrelune, and the colours go out one by one.
Stay behind me. No one else disappears tonight.

dialogue_apres.texte: Aldric… what was my husband's name again?
His name was Jorran, Maud. I'll remind you every day, if I have to.

dialogue_avant.texte: The master's door is open. That's not like him.

dialogue_apres.texte: On the table: a page torn from the Codex, and a map scribbled in haste.
“The Bridge of Mists, then the school.” What school?

dialogue_avant.texte: The only bridge still standing. Once I cross it, there's no turning back.

dialogue_apres.texte: Pierrelune, I'll be back. With the master.

dialogue_avant.texte: …forge… I had to… forge what, again…
Bram? You're the one who forged my sword…

dialogue_apres.texte: Rest now, Bram.

cinematique_apres.texte: The Hollowed collapses. For a moment, his eyes are the old blacksmith's again.
Aldric… your sword… you still hold it too high.
I know, Bram. I know.
Then the mist takes him, and the bridge finally opens before Aldric.

dialogue_avant.texte: Nice cloak, knight. You looking for an old man who draws circles in the air too?
You're talking about my master. Who are you?
Someone he owes something to. And we're surrounded, so introductions can wait.

dialogue_apres.texte: Not bad, for someone so stiff.
We travel together as far as the school. After that, we'll see.

dialogue_avant.texte: Vast ruins, covered in triangles and circles carved into the stone.
There are hundreds of names on this wall… All his students?

dialogue_apres.texte: He never told me I had brothers and sisters in arms.
He never told me much either.

dialogue_avant.texte: …circle… triangle… circle… why… why doesn't it work any more…
They still draw the signs. But there's nothing left inside them.

dialogue_apres.texte: A sign without a memory is just a gesture. The master was right.

dialogue_avant.texte: The youngest one. Did he teach you the same lesson as me? “Three gestures, not one more”?
You… you remember?
I remember everything. Except why it mattered.

dialogue_apres.texte: Then I'll remember it for both of us.

cinematique_apres.texte: Corvin falls to his knees. His grey blade cracks like glass.
He gave us everything… and we left him alone with his memories.
He's at the Heart, kid. Where everything began to fade.
Then that's where I'm going.

dialogue_avant.texte: …a student… another student… I've forgotten you all…
Master?!

fin.texte: Aldric's last sign cuts through the Silence like a ray of sunlight.
Aldric… You still hold your sword too high.
That's what Bram used to say too.
A memory fragment returns to the master.

cinematique_ouverture.texte: Vélis, the city of a thousand rooftops. And Nyra, the fastest thief of them all.
One purse, two purses… Honestly, it's almost too easy.
In her pocket, always, an old folded paper. A debt, written in a stranger's hand.
“Eldan.” One day I'll find you, old man. And we'll be even.
That night, for the first time, the guards chasing her had no faces.

dialogue_avant.texte: Guards usually shout. These ones don't say a word…

dialogue_apres.texte: Right. New rule: we don't steal from people with no faces.

dialogue_avant.texte: The great market of Vélis. The merchants no longer remember what they sell.
…apples… no… what is an apple…

dialogue_apres.texte: Old Tobbin gave me credit since I was six. He didn't even recognise me.

dialogue_avant.texte: The guild will know what to do. The guild always knows what to do.

dialogue_apres.texte: The Cats of Vélis… All of them. There's only me left.

dialogue_avant.texte: An old man was drawing circles of light near the East Gate. He said he was looking for his memories.
Eldan…

dialogue_apres.texte: East Gate. This time, the old man won't get away.

dialogue_avant.texte: …a little one… there was a little one… faster than all the others…
That was me, Sorel. That was me.

dialogue_apres.texte: My debt… not what I think? What did she mean?

cinematique_apres.texte: Madam Sorel collapses, a grey dagger still in her hand.
Nyra… your debt… it isn't what you think…
What? Sorel, wait!
Too late. The Silence has taken her back.

dialogue_avant.texte: You. You're following the same trail as me.
And you walk like a wardrobe. An old man, circles of light, ring any bells?
He's my master.
Then we've got a problem in common. And a dozen Hollowed, too.

dialogue_apres.texte: You fight well, for a wardrobe.
… Thanks?

dialogue_avant.texte: In the archives of Vélis, an old register of foundlings.
There has to be a record of my debt somewhere…

dialogue_apres.texte: “Child, four years old, saved from a fire by the traveller Eldan. Nothing owed.”
It wasn't a debt. It was a reminder. So I wouldn't forget him.

dialogue_avant.texte: They move like me… Did they learn by watching me?

dialogue_apres.texte: Copying the gestures is easy. Knowing why you make them is another story.

dialogue_avant.texte: Without him, you'd have died in the fire. Or you'd be me. Alone, fast… and empty.
Alone and fast, sure. But not empty.

dialogue_apres.texte: Goodbye, me.

cinematique_apres.texte: The Reflection shatters into a thousand shards of grey glass.
…then remember… for both of us…
That's the plan.
Far away, beyond the East Gate, a white clearing where nothing grows any more.

dialogue_avant.texte: …a little girl… a fire… I carried her… what was her name…
Nyra. Her name is Nyra, you old fool. And she's come to return the favour.

fin.texte: Nyra's dagger doesn't strike the master. It slices through the Silence around him.
Nyra… You've grown.
And you've got old. We're even now.
A memory fragment returns to the master.

cinematique_ouverture.texte: In Hautes-Gerbes, the wheat grows shoulder-high. Except on Boran.
Last sheaf of the season, big brother! After this, we sleep for a week.
You sleep. I'm fixing the barn.
As a child, Boran learned three gestures from an old traveller, as a game. He thought he'd forgotten them.
That evening, the wheat turned grey. And Oren stopped laughing.

dialogue_avant.texte: People in the field. They're walking on the wheat…
Get out of my field.

dialogue_apres.texte: Boran… I'm cold…
Oren?

dialogue_avant.texte: The neighbours he's known all his life walk towards the farm. Without a word.
Old Lucas. Mrs Anselme. I carried your flour sacks for ten years…

dialogue_apres.texte: They don't recognise me any more. But I remember them. That will count.

dialogue_avant.texte: Boran! We're all in the barn, they're going to get in!
Nobody gets in.

dialogue_apres.texte: You're the strongest in the whole world.
No. Just the heaviest.

dialogue_avant.texte: We head for the hills. Children in front, me at the back.

dialogue_apres.texte: Behind them, the farm vanishes into the grey mist. Boran doesn't look back.
Oren stayed back there.

dialogue_avant.texte: Tonnerre, the farm's bull, charges the convoy. His horns have turned to grey stone.
Tonnerre. Easy, big fella. It's me.

dialogue_apres.texte: What did I just do?

cinematique_apres.texte: Boran grabs the bull's horns and holds on. For a long time.
Then, instead of striking, he lays his hand on its forehead. The Tap.
A warm breath. For a second, Tonnerre turns brown again, and looks at him.
The old traveller's game… It wasn't a game.

dialogue_avant.texte: Don't hit him! I can still heal that one!
He's attacking us.
He's scared. That's not the same thing. Keep the others back, I'll handle the rest.

dialogue_apres.texte: The Hollowed that Mira healed looks at its hands, smiles, then gently fades away.
You saved him?
For a moment. Sometimes, a moment is already a lot.

dialogue_avant.texte: The camp is full. We need someone to guard the palisade.
I'm here.

dialogue_apres.texte: Boran, you're staying with us, right?
As long as it takes.

dialogue_avant.texte: The longest night. Boran, alone in front of the palisade.
Until dawn.

dialogue_apres.texte: The sun rises. The palisade holds. So does Boran.

dialogue_avant.texte: …a brother… I had a brother… big… slow…
Cheeky as ever, Oren.

dialogue_apres.texte: Sleep, little brother.

cinematique_apres.texte: Boran takes off his gauntlets. He doesn't want to hit anything any more.
He lays his hand on his brother's forehead, as he did with Tonnerre. The Tap.
Big brother… the barn… did you fix it?
Not yet. I was waiting for you.
Oren falls asleep, at peace. In the distance, Mira points to a white clearing.

dialogue_avant.texte: …a child… fields of wheat… I taught him a game…
It was you. The old traveller.

fin.texte: Boran doesn't strike the final blow. He holds out his hand.
The little one from Hautes-Gerbes… You've grown. You've grown a lot.
You taught me a game. It came in handy.
A memory fragment returns to the master.

cinematique_ouverture.texte: The great library of Aubelle. A hundred thousand books, and Ilwen has read nearly all of them.
Nearly. Forty-two remain. Which is frankly shameful.
Ilwen, you should get out a little. See the world.
The world is in the books, Master Aubin.
That evening, opening the forty-third book, Ilwen finds blank pages.
This book was full yesterday. Who erased the words?

dialogue_avant.texte: The shelves are emptying. The words drift away like grey dust.
No one touches my books.

dialogue_apres.texte: This isn't a thief. It's… a sickness.

dialogue_avant.texte: The erased pages… they're moving!

dialogue_apres.texte: Fascinating. Terrifying, but fascinating. I must take notes.

dialogue_avant.texte: Miss? Are you a reader? I'm the… what's my name again?
You're Master Aubin. You taught me to read.

dialogue_apres.texte: I'll find a cure. And I'll bring it back to you.

dialogue_avant.texte: Hypothesis: the three signs from the old grimoires are a cure. Method: try it.

dialogue_apres.texte: Result: it works. A little. It's a start.

dialogue_avant.texte: …file… file everything… erase what's in the way…
You guard the forbidden stacks. Stand aside.

dialogue_apres.texte: Eldan… Who are you?

cinematique_apres.texte: In the forbidden stacks, a single book has kept its words.
On the cover, a name: Eldan. And a title: The Codex of the Three Signs.
Half the pages are missing… Torn out, with care.
Someone hid this book in pieces. The others must be found.

dialogue_avant.texte: Loud. For a scholar.
And you're short on words, for a scout. That map… Show it to me.

dialogue_apres.texte: The grey zones. Been marking them for a year.
They form a circle… The Silence spreads from one precise point!

dialogue_avant.texte: We need height to be sure.
The watchtower. Three hundred steps.
… Of course.

dialogue_apres.texte: From the top, you can see everything: a white stain at the centre of the world, slowly growing.

dialogue_avant.texte: …we never taught anyone… never passed anything on…

dialogue_apres.texte: I finally understand. The Silence grows when we stop passing things on. Keeping knowledge to yourself… is already the start of forgetting it.
And to think I've never lent anyone a book.

dialogue_avant.texte: Ilwen. Always second.
Séléna. You always wrote faster than me.
I wrote everything down. And I never showed any of it to anyone. Look what's left of it.

dialogue_apres.texte: I won't make the same mistake, Séléna.

cinematique_apres.texte: Séléna's notebooks fall open. Every one of them is blank.
You… teach someone. Anyone…
I promise.
Ilwen tears a page from her own grimoire and hands it to Kestrel. The first knowledge she has ever shared.

dialogue_avant.texte: …a book… I hid a book… in pieces… inside my head…
The Codex. You hid it in your memory. And in the end, your memory closed in on you.

fin.texte: Ilwen opens her grimoire and reads the recovered pages aloud.
These words… they're mine.
I know. I've reread them forty-three times.
A memory fragment returns to the master.

cinematique_ouverture.texte: The Pass Scouts. Their mission: to map the world. Their best recruit: Kestrel.
Kestrel. You go on ahead. As usual.
As usual.
For a year now, Kestrel's map has been filling with grey patches. Nobody knows what they are.
They're growing.
Then mark them down. A good map is what separates the living from the lost.

dialogue_avant.texte: Something's moving in the grey trees.

dialogue_apres.texte: Hostile. Noted.

dialogue_avant.texte: Back at camp, at night. Too quiet.
Captain?

dialogue_apres.texte: Camp's empty. Captain's gone.

dialogue_avant.texte: My map. Torn. Pieces everywhere.

dialogue_apres.texte: Piece by piece, Kestrel puts a year of work back together.
It's all here. Almost.

dialogue_avant.texte: The pass is closing. Now or never.

dialogue_apres.texte: Through. Barely.

dialogue_avant.texte: For three days, a grey figure has been on Kestrel's trail.
You're good. Not good enough.

dialogue_apres.texte: I won't leave anyone behind again.

cinematique_apres.texte: The Tracker falls. Around his neck, a badge of the Pass Scouts.
Pieter… You were in my unit.
He wasn't hunting her. He was trying to follow her, like before, without knowing why.
Rest. I'll go on for both of us.

dialogue_avant.texte: You there! Your map. I need it.
No.
It's for science!
Then follow me. And be quiet.

dialogue_apres.texte: You are extremely unpleasant.
But I've got the map.

dialogue_avant.texte: All the zones converge. One point.

dialogue_apres.texte: At the centre of the map, Kestrel draws a star. Then she hesitates, and writes: “Heart”.

dialogue_avant.texte: The trees are vanishing behind us. Don't look back.

dialogue_apres.texte: No way back. Good. Keep moving.

dialogue_avant.texte: …a recruit… the best one… she always went on ahead…
Captain. It's me.

dialogue_apres.texte: I'll finish it for you, Captain.

cinematique_apres.texte: Captain Hardel drops to one knee. In his hand, an old compass.
Kestrel… a good map… separates the living… from the lost…
I know, Captain.
The compass no longer points north. It points to the Heart.

dialogue_avant.texte: …so many paths… I don't know which one leads home any more…
I do. I've got the map.

fin.texte: Kestrel unrolls her map before the master. A year of work.
It's… every step of the way I've travelled.
Then you're not lost any more.
A memory fragment returns to the master.

cinematique_ouverture.texte: Fontclaire, its clear water, and its little house of healing at the end of the lane.
Some tea for that cough, a balm for those knees, and a smile for everyone!
Mira, you heal too fast. One day, you'll come across something you can't cure.
Then I'll keep looking until I find the cure!
That morning, her first patient could no longer remember why he had come.
Mr Fabre? You came about your back… do you remember?

dialogue_avant.texte: One by one, the patients turn grey.
Everyone stay calm! Nobody leaves the waiting room!

dialogue_apres.texte: They don't know who they are any more… This isn't a sickness I know.

dialogue_avant.texte: The Silence spreads through Fontclaire like a fever.

dialogue_apres.texte: Herbal tea won't fix this. I need something else.

dialogue_avant.texte: Grandma used to say: “A hand laid in the right place heals more than any remedy.” Let's try.

dialogue_apres.texte: … Mira? My back hurts.
He remembers! He remembers his back!
Then the grey slowly returns. But Mira has seen what she needed to see.

dialogue_avant.texte: If it works here, it'll work elsewhere. Let's go!

dialogue_apres.texte: Three villages, eleven memories given back! Just a few seconds each time, fine. But it's a start!

dialogue_avant.texte: …plants… I knew every plant…
Aunt Hélo… You're the one who taught me everything.

dialogue_apres.texte: Heal the ones I can. Remember the others. All right.

cinematique_apres.texte: Mira lays both hands on her mentor's forehead.
Mira… You still heal too fast.
And you were right. Some of them, I can't cure.
Then heal the ones you can. And remember the others.

dialogue_avant.texte: Stop! Don't hit that one!
He's attacking us.
Because he's scared. Cover me, big guy!

dialogue_apres.texte: You saved him?
For a moment. And a moment is already a memory.

dialogue_avant.texte: Two hundred refugees, one single guard. Luckily, he counts for ten.

dialogue_apres.texte: In the healing tent, Mira works all night. Outside, Boran keeps watch.

dialogue_avant.texte: Some Hollowed no longer respond to the Tap. Not at all.

dialogue_apres.texte: I can't save them all.
No. But you remember them. That counts.
… That's my line.

dialogue_avant.texte: Why make them suffer, healer? Forgetting doesn't hurt. I bring them relief.
You're not bringing them relief. You're erasing them.

dialogue_apres.texte: I'm going to the Heart.

cinematique_apres.texte: The Watcher staggers. Beneath her grey hood, the face of a former nurse.
I only wanted… no one to hurt any more…
I know. Me too. But pain is part of our memories.
Mira holds her hand until the very end. Then she stands, and walks towards the Heart.

dialogue_avant.texte: …it hurts… to remember… let me forget…
No. Not you. You, I can still heal.

fin.texte: Mira lays her hands on the master's forehead. The Tap, with all her strength.
It's warm… like herbal tea…
With honey. That's the secret.
A memory fragment returns to the master.

prologue_commun.texte: Long ago, three simple gestures protected people: the Circle to guard, the Triangle to strike, the Tap to heal and connect.
They were called the Imprint. An old master, Eldan, taught them to anyone willing to learn.
Then the Silence came. It didn't break down doors: it erased memories.
Those who forget everything become the Hollowed. Grey, empty shapes… who were never monsters.
Six people still remember the three signs. These are their stories.

cinematique.texte: At the centre of the world, a white clearing. No wind, no sound, no colour.
In the middle, an old man draws signs in the empty air. Again, and again.
Circle… triangle… tap… What was it all for, again?
Six fragments. Six heroes. And at last, a whole memory.
My name is Eldan. I am… I was… a master.
And you owe us an explanation.
Then sit down. It's a long story. And this time, I'm going to pass it on.
New character unlocked: Eldan, the Master. His story is coming soon.
